title: Set up a patient's oxygen at 2 L/min: push the cannula tubing onto the flowmeter's nipple, turn the knob to the line
instruction: Set up the patient's oxygen at 2 L/min. Push the nasal cannula's tubing fully onto the flowmeter's outlet nipple, then turn the flowmeter's knob until the middle of the float ball is on the 2 L/min line, and let go of both.
context: Registered nurses set up oxygen for patients every shift. Open RN, Nursing Skills, 4.6 Checklist for Oxygen Therapy: "Connect nasal cannula tubing to flow meter.", "Set oxygen flow at prescribed rate." Ohio Medical, Medical Gas Flowmeters IFU: "To set the flow, align the center of the Float Ball to the indicator line on the Flow Tube." Done by: registered nurses (BLS: 3,465,400 jobs in 2025; duties include "Administer patients' medicines and treatments"), licensed practical nurses and respiratory therapists.
setup: Positions in cm on the table, from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left. A 0-15 L/min wall oxygen flowmeter (152 mm tall, 56 mm wide, 58 mm deep) is plugged into the green oxygen outlet of a headwall panel (24 x 30 cm, its face at x 38.6), fixed, its front face at x 31, centred on y 0, from 7 to 22.2 cm above the table, turned off. On its front: a clear flow tube with a float ball 8 mm across (lines every 0.5 L/min from 1 to 5 and every 1 L/min from 5 to 15, numbered 1-5, 10, 15; the ball's middle rests 10.4 cm up, the 2 L/min line 2 cm higher), a green fluted flow-control knob 27 mm across at the top (its axis 21.2 cm up, its front at x 29; anticlockwise from the front opens it), and at the bottom a green barbed tubing nipple, 20 mm long (three barbs 6 mm across, its tip 3.6 mm), pointing towards the arms (its axis 8.4 cm up, its tip at x 27.5). The end of a nasal cannula's oxygen tubing (15 cm, clear green, 8 mm across, a 5 mm bore) lies along x on the cannula's opened packet (10 x 7 x 2.5 cm, centred at (9.5, -10)), its open end towards the flowmeter at (20, -10), 2.9 cm up, 55 mm over the packet's edge. Both grippers start open at the ready pose. Real trials: an Ohio Medical 6703-1260-921 flowmeter (DISS inlet, tubing nipple outlet) screwed onto a DISS outlet in the panel, fed at 50 psi through a DISS oxygen hose from the regulator of a size E medical oxygen cylinder chained in a stand beside the table; parts, safety and checks in the README (Real trials).
scoring: From the two models and the parts' poses, at the end. Seated: the tubing's open end 15 mm or more onto the nipple (past its last barb's crest), within 1.5 mm of its axis and 10 degrees of its line as it goes on. The flow follows the knob's angle (2 L/min at 36 degrees open). 1.0: seated, the flow within 0.25 L/min of 2 (the ball's middle within 2.5 mm of the 2 L/min line), and both grippers more than 2 cm from the tubing and the knob, held 1 s (0.9 if time runs out first). 0.5: seated, the flow on (0.1 to 4 L/min) but off the line. 0.25: seated with the flow off, or the flow on the line with the tubing not seated. 0 otherwise, and for any flow over 4 L/min.
reset_notes: Turn the knob fully clockwise (off), pull the tubing off the nipple and lay it back on the packet, its open end 55 mm over the edge. Real trials: every 10 trials cut 1 cm off the tubing's end (the stretched end loosens) and check its push-on force with a force gauge (README, Real trials); at the end of a session close the cylinder valve and bleed the regulator.
fidelity: No oxygen flows: the knob's angle sets the flow (15 L/min at 270 degrees, our estimate) and the ball rides on its line. The flowmeter is fixed at table height. The tubing's end is rigid, 15 cm, 40 g. Its stretch over the barbs is a model: centred on the nipple, it pushes back up to 4.4, 8.8, then 13.2 N over the three barbs (our estimate from the sizes and 70 Shore A PVC, barbfit.py), so a weaker push doesn't move it; seated, it is held.
